commit.message:
Record version 2 of arXiv:2608.12543, and withdraw a comparison

Version 2 of 31 August 2026 renames the paper to Collision-Generated
Compression for Homogeneous Keller Maps, drops the forty-variable
counterexample from the title, and renames its ancillary file. Lemma 2
and Theorem 3 keep their numbers and their statements, so nothing this
library builds against has moved.

It falsifies a sentence on docs/references.md. The nineteen cubic
homogeneous variables the pipeline of 0.6 reaches were described there as
one below the smallest figure the page records, Macfarlane's twenty, with
the note that the literature had been checked and nothing smaller found.
Version 2 records a published nineteen: van Rijn's twelve-variable
degree-three map, rank-compressed and homogenized. The paragraph now says
that nineteen is no longer below anything published and that it said it
was.

Whether that nineteen is the one this pipeline reaches is left open. The
two arrive by different routes and this page does not compare maps it has
not compared. Saying so is cheaper than a comparison that would have to
be made before it could be claimed.

What version 2 adds is recorded rather than summarised away: the
collision-generated sequence of that map is 2, 4, 11, 19, 19, so the hull
is the whole space, and Proposition 8 draws the consequence that no proper
invariant linear restriction retaining the collision lowers the
thirty-eight-variable lift in any codimension. The lift is written out
with 340 monomials against the 350 of the forty-variable one. Both
minimality statements in that paper are route-specific and neither is
global; the page repeats that because the distinction is the one this
project has got wrong before.

Two five-variable examples the new version names are set aside on the page
with the reason: one is not a homogeneous Hessian-nilpotent quartic and
the other uses a third-order operator rather than the Laplacian, so
neither variable count is comparable with the quartic problem.

Version 2 cites this project by name, as an independent computational
uptake of the construction. The page records it and says what it is not:
a citation that the construction was used, not a second opinion on
anything in this repository. What was checked here is what
docs/provenance.md lists.

The citations move by what they are for. Those that name a theorem --
kellermap.compression, kellermap.lift, the CHC and SYM sections of the
contract page, architecture.md, api.md, test_lift.py -- name version 2.
Those that record where fixed data was transcribed from stay at version 1
and name its ancillary file, because a transcription is from the bytes it
was made from: examples.py, provenance.md, and the reconstruction script,
whose docstring now says why it stays and that both figures it checks are
unchanged in version 2. The errata, changelog and roadmap entries that
record what was said at a time stay as they are.

Gates: ruff format --check, ruff check, mypy src, mypy --strict scripts,
pytest (1893 passed, 16 deselected), make reconstruct (16 of 16). The
reconstruction still agrees, which is what says Theorem 3 did not move.

commit.message:
Refresh four statements that a milestone had outlived

Work package 12 of milestone 0.7, the last of the corrections the audit
of 0.7.0rc1 asked for. Documentation and one line of metadata; no code.

docs/references.md said Proposition (3.1) delivers part (b) of Theorem
2.1 "in a second half this library does not implement". That stopped
being true in work package 2.1 of this milestone, and work package 2
edited the sentence beside it without seeing the clause. The paragraph
now says which function reaches the first half, that HOM-11 and HOM-12
check both at the end of the chain, and that a chain not asked for the
refinement still ends cubic homogeneous -- with the figure for the
smallest case, where the refinement takes (x + y^3, y) to a verified
thirteen against the five it reaches without.

A second paragraph said the library carries out neither of the two
stages that lead to the cubic homogeneous form, so it had no certified
figure there and claimed none, and called 27 and 22 for alpoege13 a
target for the packages of 0.6. Those packages were built. Both figures
are certified now and make measure recomputes them against this page.
What the certificate adds is the determinant as a polynomial, which the
plain-SymPy measurement did not check; what it does not add is priority
or minimality, and the paragraph says so and points at docs/errata.md
for the time this project read more into such a comparison than it
establishes.

The abstract of CITATION.cff described milestone 0.6 and now names 0.7
with 0.6 behind it. The description in pyproject.toml said the project
was working towards the reduction, which it has carried out since 0.6
and completed in this milestone.

That both references.md paragraphs were a milestone out of date is worth
a note rather than a shrug. Neither is under a gate that could notice:
make measure checks the figures on that page and not the sentences
around them, and no test reads a paragraph for a claim about what
exists. The audits have found every one of these.

commit.message:
Probe the descent

Work package 11 of milestone 0.7, the fourth of the corrections the
audit of 0.7.0rc1 asked for. Three probes, which makes forty-five.

Milestone 0.7 added ten obligations and only three take a probe. DSC-3
in both halves and DSC-4 in the half that is about arithmetic are the
clauses the contract page names as able to fail on data a caller
supplies, and they are here. HOM-11 and HOM-12 cannot fail after HOM-1,
which that page argues where it says which of the HOM family can fail,
so a probe for either would report a miss for a reason that is not a
missing control. UNT-12 is an enumerator and offers rather than
certifies, which is why no UNT clause has ever had one. The audit
reached the same conclusion about HOM-11 and HOM-12 and asked for the
DSC ones.

All three report CAUGHT against the current tree, which is what every
probe here should do. tests/test_scripts.py holds each fragment against
the code it aims at, so a later edit that moves one of these lines fails
the suite rather than turning the probe into a silent no-op.

The count is stated in three places and all three move.
scripts/mutation_probe.py carries the running tally by milestone;
docs/provenance.md lists the sweep among what was verified rather than
trusted. docs/deposit.md names it in a sentence about the six audits of
0.6, so the count there is scoped to that release rather than raised --
it was forty-two at the time and saying so is what keeps the sentence
true.
